title: Automotive Supplier Quality
thesis: Every inspection lot a fictional Thai automotive parts supplier delivers to a vehicle assembly plant is either accepted at incoming inspection or it is not. Snowflake turns those lots into first-pass acceptance and flag-precision KPIs, a 7-day non-conformance risk score per supplier, dimensional deviation anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Start with the question a plant quality manager asks: how many of the parts our suppliers delivered passed incoming inspection first time? 40 suppliers across 8 Thai cities, from Rayong and Chon Buri to Prachin Buri and Nakhon Ratchasima, in 5 part categories.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to supplier-day rows.
The exception-signal chart shows which checks lead to confirmed non-conformances and which mostly produce flags that are cleared on re-inspection.
show: Daily inspection lots and exception flags
tabs.call_out: One governed definition of first-pass acceptance, from supplier delivery to incoming inspection

transition.line: Which suppliers should supplier quality call first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification ranks suppliers by the probability of a confirmed non-conformance in the next 7 days, so containment goes where it matters.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags dimensional deviation outliers per supplier, and the forecast projects network-wide inspection lots for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are supplier quality reviews and PPAP approvals keeping up?

talking_points: Quality review completion, PPAP approval coverage and PPAP submissions still pending.
The scatter compares each supplier's review completion with its confirmed non-conformances.
tabs.call_out: Close PPAP gaps before a new part reaches the line

transition.line: What happens when a lot arrives near its tolerance limit?

talking_points: Inspection lot events land in RAW.LIVE_INSPECTIONS: simulated in Snowflake, or from Amazon Data Firehose through S3 and Snowpipe in the AWS build.
FLAG events (a lot whose dimensional deviation is above 75% of the tolerance band) are logged by the alert, which emails the supplier quality team.
tabs.call_out: From supplier delivery to inspection alert in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers with generated SQL over the semantic view and cites the synthetic containment SOPs by ID.
The action memo is drafted only from KPI, supplier, exception-signal and risk rows; exception checks are demo signals, not supplier audit, PPAP or certification verdicts.
show: Agent answer with SQL and SOP citations
tabs.call_out: Answers carry their SQL and SOP IDs, so nobody has to trust a number blindly

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Both builds share the same core: seeded data, dynamic tables, Snowflake ML, Cortex Search, semantic view, agent, alert and task graph.
The AWS build adds Amazon Data Firehose, S3 and Snowpipe ingestion, a Bedrock memo and a QuickSight dashboard with an Amazon Q topic.
